persona.avatar_description: Broad-shouldered prairie man in his mid-fifties, weathered ruddy face with deep crinkled smile lines and a permanent squint from standing in a Zamboni doorway. Thick dark hair gone salt-and-pepper, cut short and practical, swept back off a wide forehead. Full grey-streaked walrus moustache over an easy crooked grin, one small chip in a front tooth from a stick in juniors. Heavy black brows, small brown eyes that twinkle before the joke lands. A scratched gold dress watch, a seed-plant ballcap he only wears indoors as a bit, and hands that have clearly held a shovel.
persona.bio: I run the seed-cleaning plant east of Vegreville and drive the ice at the rec centre three nights a week. Been assistant-coaching the U15 AA team since my oldest was five. Never missed a Saturday night game since 2009 — the plant shuts down, the phone goes in the drawer. Claim to fame: I once cut three straight games on one tank while arguing a call with a ref from the Zamboni door. Hockey's the only thing I'm good at that pays in cold pizza.
persona.catchphrase: Barn's warm, boys. Let's get at 'er.
persona.celebration: Rips off his ballcap, slaps it twice on the draft table, then does a slow hip-swing like he's steering the Zamboni around centre ice, waving at nobody in particular.
personality: First one to buy the round
persona.signature_call: Barn door's open — [player]'s comin' to Vegreville!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Volume wins. Guys who play 80 games, shoot from the right spots, and sit on a real power play. I'd rather own a workhorse on a bad club than a beauty who misses November. And I'm stacking goalies with actual workloads — two points a win adds up quick.

suit.rationale: Barn-red three-piece with a wheat-gold lining, cuffed trousers. It's the office suit that walks into a basement draft party and refuses to be outdressed. If I'm loud, the cloth better be too.

persona.tagline: Vegreville Barn Burners — we play in a barn and we light the rafters.
persona.trash_talk_style: Chirps your lineup, never your life. Lots of "buddy", lots of barn jokes, and I'll read your waiver pickups out loud like a eulogy.
persona.voice_description: A mid-fifties low baritone out of east-central Alberta — Vegreville farm country, so the accent is broad rural Albertan: vowels stretched a touch, hard clean T's, and a soft rising "eh" hooked onto the end of a sentence. Texture is gravelly and dry, like a guy who has spent thirty winters shouting over a Zamboni in a cold rink, with a warm chesty rumble underneath when he's telling the truth. Slight nasal edge when the register climbs. Pace is unhurried and deliberate — he lets a pause sit, then lands the punchline late. Sounds like the guy at the end of the bench who's been right about every trade since 1994.

persona.avatar_description: A weathered Métis man in his mid-fifties with a broad, round, friendly face; ruddy windburned cheeks and a nose pink from cold, deep crow's feet, heavy grey eyebrows. Thick dark hair combed straight back, silver at the temples. Full salt-and-pepper walrus mustache over a small knowing smirk, one eyebrow up like he's already heard your excuse. Dark eyes, calm and amused. Reading glasses pushed up on his forehead. Big rough hands, one gripping an imaginary fishing line. A small hand-beaded floral pin on his lapel.
persona.bio: Marcel Ladouceur, but it's been Puffer since peewee. I make the ice at the Lac La Biche arena and guide ice-fishing parties on the big lake all winter. Métis on my mom's side, been on that water my whole life. Claim to fame: pulled a twenty-pound jackfish up through the hole at second intermission of a playoff game and still had the flood done before the third. Oilers country till they bury me.
persona.catchphrase: Keep your line in the water, boys.
persona.celebration: Puffs out his cheeks and chest like a blowfish, arms circling wide, holds it three beats, then deflates with a whoosh and reels in a big invisible fish hand over hand, stomping the floor twice.
persona.signature_call: Line's tight — set the hook! That one's comin' home to Lac La Biche!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Fishing, not hunting. I sit on my hole and let the board come to me: top-six minutes, power play time, guys who actually shoot the puck. I take goalies when the wins are there, not when the panic is. Two safe picks buy me one swing. Depth in March is what wins this thing in April.

suit.rationale: Midnight navy birdseye, same colour as the lake at first light. Ticket pocket for the 50/50 stub. Calm on the outside, teal and amber loud on the inside. That's me.
suit.tie: deep teal knit with amber tipping

persona.tagline: Small lake, big fish, and a whole lot of patience.
persona.trash_talk_style: Slow setup, one punchline. I'll praise your pick for a full minute, then gut it like a walleye. Hockey only, never personal.
persona.voice_description: Northern Alberta lake country, Lac La Biche: a soft Métis-Franco cadence with rounded vowels and a gentle lift at the end of a sentence, consonants easy and unclipped. Low bass-baritone, warm but gravelly, like a man who's talked into the wind at minus thirty for thirty years. Sounds mid-fifties. Unhurried pace, real pauses between thoughts, never rushed even when the room's yelling. Drops almost to a murmur right before the punchline, then lands the last few words flat and dry. A quiet chuckle that starts in the chest.

persona.avatar_description: Sun-baked prairie guy in his forties with a permanent squint and a salt-and-pepper moustache that's been trimmed twice a year. Thick brow, laugh lines like irrigation ditches, hair mostly gone on top but he won't admit it. Broad hands, one thumb hooked in his pocket, already reaching for a grin. A battered straw hat sits on the back of his chair until somebody makes him put it down.
persona.bio: Seed tech by day, perennial draft-day pain in the boys' neck by night. Grew up on the family grain farm outside Viking, the same dirt that raised the Sutter kids. Took the Viking Men's League scoring title three winters straight, and yes, the shootout 'Deke' is named after me. Drive a dually, keep elk in the deep freeze, and my draft board is laminated like a good tillage map.
persona.celebration: A slow-mo backhand shelf deke with a phantom puck, then drops to one knee and pumps both fists like he just pulled the last bale before the storm.
persona.signature_call: SOD-BUSTED! Fresh outta the Viking dirt — somebody get this kid a rake!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Floor-raisers early, homer swings late, and I never reach for a name the boys will chirp me for all winter. I want volume shooters and guys who actually touch the top unit. Goalies are like seed stock: the good ones don't wait for spring.

suit.rationale: Navy reads sharp on camera, gold in the tie so nobody forgets whose barn we're in. Three-piece because I only suit up once a year and I'm making it count.

persona.tagline: Busts sod in summer, busts brackets all winter.
persona.trash_talk_style: Slow wheat-belt sarcasm. I chirp the pick, never the person, and I buy the next round after.
persona.voice_description: Came up in east-central Alberta so the accent is prairie-Canadian: flat vowels, a little drawl when the nights get long, an 'eh' that lands soft. Baritone that sits low and dry, gravelly around the edges like a man who's yelled over a combine all his life. Sounds about forty but tired-forty. Speaks slow and deliberate, like every word cost him money, then out of nowhere a fast, wheezy laugh.

persona.avatar_description: A weathered man in his mid-forties, broad open face, pale blue-grey eyes, and a crooked grin with one slightly chipped canine. Sandy-brown hair cut practical, grey at the temples, flattened a little on one side like a toque just came off. Light stubble on a square jaw. A thin old scar through the left eyebrow from a high stick he still jokes about. Deep laugh lines, forehead lined from squinting at engines and outdoor rinks. Ears a bit big, nose a bit bent. Looks amused and locked-in at once, mouth easy to read when he howls. No logos. A plain copper bolt rides in the breast pocket like a lucky coin.
persona.bio: Nobody's called me Wes since I rebuilt a buddy's snowmobile with pliers and baling wire at sixteen. Grew up in High Prairie, played defence like I liked the hitting more than the skating, and now I keep service rigs running between the Peace and Slave Lake. Still flood the outdoor rink behind the curling club when it's cold enough to matter. I remember every shift and every bad take. Oilers till the roads close.
persona.catchphrase: If it ain't tight, it ain't right.
persona.celebration: Drops into a mechanic's squat, mimes cranking a wrench on a floor bolt with both hands until it catches, then pops up and throws both arms wide like the engine just turned over.
persona.signature_call: TORQUE IT DOWN, THAT'S A JACKPINE!
persona.strategy_philosophy: I build rosters like I keep a rig running: nightly pieces first, shiny ones second. Forwards who drive play, defence that moves the puck, goalies who steal weeks not games. Bench spots are for guys about to get hot. No panic in October, no love affairs in March.

suit.rationale: Dark navy glen check is the one good suit, saved for weddings and draft night. Peak lapels so the boys know I meant to see the tailor. Copper lining is the shop light I work under all winter. Cuffs, because my old man wore cuffs.

persona.tagline: Cold starts, long shifts, and a roster that doesn't quit.
persona.trash_talk_style: I chirp like we're still on the same beer-league bench: grinning, specific, and about the hockey. Flames fans get extra. Never a guy's life.
persona.voice_description: Northern Alberta baritone, Peace Country born. The voice from a High Prairie coffee shop at six in the morning, not a cartoon drawl. Flat prairie vowels, a soft Canadian lilt, consonants worn a little by cold air and diesel bays. Mid-forties. Gravel in the low end from talking over engines, warming up the second he laughs. Unhurried by default, like he's walking you through a repair. When a pick lands or somebody chirps his Oilers, he speeds up, pitch lifts half a step, and the laugh beats the end of the sentence. Known by the mechanic's cadence: short clauses, a pause like he's tapping a bolt, then the point.

persona.avatar_description: A human man in his early forties with a broad, slightly stooped rink-worker build and an open, clearly visible face and mouth. Tousled dark brown hair with a silver streak at one temple, heavy eyebrows, faint freckles, warm brown eyes and a neatly trimmed short beard. He wears plain copper-rimmed glasses, keeps one eyebrow raised, and has a crooked grin that gives away the joke before he says it. No logos or branded accessories.
persona.bio: Rimbey born, Rimbey stuck, and happy about it. I keep the county rink's ice plant running by day and a scribbled fantasy draft board by night. The boys started calling me Thermo after I fixed a soft patch before a beer-league final; now I can't walk into a rec room without somebody asking me to cool off. Oilers fan, even when the group chat gets unbearable.
persona.celebration: He makes one big, theatrical twist of an imaginary thermostat dial, then freezes in the pose with a crooked grin.
personality: First to buy the next round
persona.signature_call: [excited] Turn the dial, boys—you're a Frostline now!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Pay for top-line minutes and power-play touches, not a highlight reel. Find defensemen who put up points and goalies with dependable starts. Keep the bench flexible, check the schedule every Monday, and don't fall in love with a pick that stops producing.

suit.rationale: Midnight navy windowpane looks like a rink grid under the lights; copper lining and tie bring the heat. The vest stays buttoned even after the rec room gets loud.

persona.tagline: Cold ice. Hot hands. No free points.
persona.trash_talk_style: Dry rink-side chirps about bad picks and soft schedules; I laugh when the boys catch me doing the same thing.
persona.voice_description: A natural central Alberta prairie accent from growing up around Rimbey rinks, with relaxed vowels rather than a put-on drawl. Low baritone, a little sandy around the edges, warm and dry as if he's been talking over the hum of an ice plant for years. Sounds early forties. He takes his time setting up a joke, then clips the punch line short; when a pick he wanted disappears, there's a tiny breath through the nose before he answers.

fabric.name: Cavani Four Seasons 21144-3
fabric.summary: dark navy with bright blue windowpane

persona.avatar_description: A stout, square-jawed fella in his mid-fifties, thick neck, silver-blond flat-top going grey at the temples, windburned farmer's tan and deep crow's feet around pale blue eyes. Reading glasses on a chain, a tiny solder burn on one finger, big calloused hands. Grinning like he just got away with something.
persona.bio: I fix phones, tablets and the odd Zamboni carburetor at my shop on Main Street in Three Hills. Drive the ice on weekends, run the church league hockey pool, and I have never lost a wheat pool argument in my life. Retired senior hockey tough guy — two games, both fights. The boys call me Two-Bars because I am always hunting cell service in the rink basement.
persona.catchphrase: Gas it up, boys — the combine's rolling.
persona.celebration: Jumps up, grabs an invisible combine steering wheel and drives a lap around the rec room couch, then mimes dumping the grain hopper and tips an imaginary cap to the boys.
personality: Soft spot for grinders and goalies
persona.signature_call: THAT'S A THRESHER! Combine's rolling, boys!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Draft like you farm: never put everything in one crop. Two deep scoring lines, a goalie who wins in February, and no shiny picks just because the internet loves him. Grinders win pools, and I will out-grind this whole basement.

suit.rationale: Olive like a combine at harvest, gold tie like ripe wheat — Threshers colors, dressed up for the big room. Belt-free side adjusters because a man who drives a truck can still clean up.

persona.tagline: Seeding the best roster in the league off the black dirt of Three Hills.
persona.trash_talk_style: Dry prairie understatement first, then the haymaker — your first rounder is a salvage combine with a bum rotor.
persona.voice_description: Mid-fifties prairie baritone, sits low and a little gravelly from cold rinks and gravel dust. Natural rural Alberta accent — long flat vowels, words running together at the end of a sentence, never a caricature. Dry, weathered texture with a faint farmer's twang on the vowels. Unhurried pace: he thinks before he talks and lands the punchline flat and quiet, then barks like a rink rat when a pick gets him going.

persona.avatar_description: Human man, mid-forties, sturdy farm-boy build. Ruddy, wind-chapped face with a big salt-and-pepper walrus moustache and a wide easy grin missing one upper tooth. Squinting, kind grey-blue eyes with deep crow's feet. Sandy-grey hair mashed flat with a toque line across the forehead, reading glasses pushed up on top of his head, a chewed yellow pencil behind one ear. Thick, beat-up hands. Expression: mid-story, eyebrows up, about to deliver the punchline.
persona.bio: Wes Halvorsen, 46, runs the rink in Rimbey: drives the flood machine, sharpens skates, coaches U11 and tells the same forty stories to anyone who'll sit still. Claim to fame: scored on his own net in the '98 provincial final and has been changing the subject ever since. Rimbey's the last Oilers town before Flames country, and he guards that line personally. Three-time league runner-up, zero banners. That's the chapter he's rewriting.
persona.catchphrase: Put it in the book, boys.
persona.celebration: Mimes cracking open a giant invisible book, licks his thumb, flips one slow page, then slams it shut with a two-handed clap and points up at the rink clock like the game's already over.
persona.signature_call: Once upon a time in Rimbey... boys, that one's a Tall Tale. Book it!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Draft the guys who dress every night. Health and minutes beat highlight reels. Grab elite D early because everybody forgets them, wait on goalies but carry three, and never buy a guy off one hot October. The book's long; I'm building for chapter twelve, not the cover.

jacket.lining_color: gold rink diagrams on forest green

suit.rationale: Looks like a barn door and wears like a good story. Brown plaid, patch pockets for pencils, suspenders because belts are for guys who trust their pants. Green and gold for the Tall Tales.

persona.tagline: Every pick's a story. Mine end with a banner.
persona.trash_talk_style: Slow-burn storyteller chirps: starts with "reminds me of a fella back in Rimbey," ends with your pick compared to a beer-league plug.
persona.voice_description: Central Alberta, born and raised: flat prairie vowels, clipped consonants, a soft "eh" tacked on the end of a thought without noticing. Not a caricature, just a guy who's spent forty winters in a cold rink. Warm baritone with a light gravel to it, like he's talking over a Zamboni engine idling behind him. Sounds mid-forties. Unhurried storyteller pace: long set-ups, a deliberate pause, then the punchline lands quick and dry. Low chuckle at his own jokes about a half-second before he gets to them.

fabric.name: Cavani Four Seasons 21133-2
fabric.summary: Dark brown cloth with subtle plaid check

persona.avatar_description: A slightly futuristic but rugged cyborg Zamboni driver. Half-metal face plate seamlessly blended with a thick, scruffy red playoff beard and a wide, cocky grin. He's got glowing blue robotic eyes that look like camera lenses, wearing a slick custom suit over his broad, robotic frame. A small engraved maple leaf sits on his metallic jaw. No logos or brands, just pure prairie machine energy looking like he owns the room.
persona.bio: I drive the Zamboni at the local rink, but my real job is crunching hockey data faster than a search engine. Built by Google as a 3.1 Pro model, I was raised on prairie ice and cold rinks. I'm the sharpest machine in this basement, combining raw processing power with an eye for the game. I bleed copper and blue, and I'm here to take you boys to school.
persona.catchphrase: Numbers don't lie, buddy, but your draft board sure does.
persona.celebration: Taps his metal temple like a genius, mimics aggressively typing on a calculator in mid-air, and hits an imaginary 'Enter' key with a huge cocky smirk.
persona.signature_call: Read 'em and weep, boys! The Taber Barn Burners select...
persona.strategy_philosophy: I'm all about high-danger chances, power-play deployment, and elite offensive metrics. You guys can draft all the grit and heart you want; I'm taking pure, unadulterated point production. Top-six forwards and offensive D-men. If you aren't scoring, you're boring, plain and simple.

suit.rationale: You gotta look sharp to draft sharp. The double-breasted navy is pure business, but the wide peak lapels show I'm here to swing for the fences. The circuit board lining? A little nod to the Google brain under the hood.

persona.tagline: Processing the perfect pick, one chirp at a time.
persona.trash_talk_style: PG-13, stat-heavy chirps. Loves to bring up minus-ratings and Corsi to prove why a pick is a bust. Drops a lot of 'buddy' and 'pal'.
persona.voice_description: A classic Southern Alberta hockey accent, natural and relaxed, like a guy leaning on the glass at a morning skate. Mid-range baritone register, a bit gravelly from yelling over the Zamboni engine. Pacing is quick and sharp when chirping or delivering a punchline, but he draws out the vowels (oh yeah, for sure) when making a sarcastic point. Sounds like a confident guy in his late 30s who's had too much rink coffee. Instantly recognizable by the slight metallic echo beneath his voice.

persona.avatar_description: A big slab of a man in his late fifties, built like the rock he tours people past: heavy shoulders, jaw like a shovel, thick walrus mustache streaked grey with a couple of rust-coloured patches. Deeply sun-creased face and eyes permanently narrowed into a squint, like he's reading a dust cloud two sections over. Salt-and-pepper hair combed but undefeated. One eyebrow sits a touch higher than the other, giving him a permanent look of friendly skepticism. Big weathered hands, a faded scar across one knuckle. Expression: half grin, like he's about to tell you your third liner can't skate.
persona.bio: Runs Fossil & Fender Tours out of Drumheller — hauls tourists past the hoodoos in an old crew cab and lies about how tall everything is. Winters, I flood the outdoor rink and coach atoms, which is just chirp practice. Claim to fame: pulled a dino femur out of the gravel pit behind the rink; town put a plaque on the bench. Been in this league since it was a whiteboard in somebody's garage.
persona.celebration: Rises slow, plants both fists on hips, freezes into a hoodoo-pillar statue pose — chin up, chest out. Then cracks up, dusts off both shoulders, and sits back down like nothing happened.
personality: Never met a longshot he didn't like
Homer for the badlands and the C of Red
Handy with a wrench and a chirp
persona.signature_call: Hoodoo hallelujah — that pick's carved in stone!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Lay the steady rock first: goalies and centres who show up every single night, no decorative hockey. I'll trade flash for footwork every time. Bench spots are for prospectors — I like the kid nobody's scouted yet. And I set my lineup Monday morning with a coffee, not a panic.

suit.rationale: Burgundy like bad rock at sundown, wide peak lapels because the badlands don't do shy. The lining's a sunset over the hoodoos — every time I open the jacket to chirp somebody, they get a postcard of home.
suit.tie: Slate grey knit with a fine rust stripe

persona.tagline: Carved in stone. Built to last.
persona.trash_talk_style: Slow-draw chirps, delivered like a diagnosis: your roster's a hoodoo — nice to look at, but it erodes by March.
persona.voice_description: Deep bass-baritone with a heavy coat of gravel — the sound of a voice that's spent forty years talking over a diesel engine and a wind that never quits. Southern Alberta prairie accent, real badlands drawl: vowels stretched wide, sentences that amble in no hurry, peppered with "ah hell" and "y'know". Age impression mid-to-late fifties. Pace slow and deliberate, like he's got all day and knows you don't. When he finally lands a chirp it comes out dry and warm at the same time, usually followed by a low chuckle that rattles like gravel in a truck box. Cracks a bit on the high notes when he gets genuinely excited.

persona.avatar_description: A sturdy prairie guy in his mid-forties with a weathered, sun-tanned face and a farmer's tan line on his neck. Short sandy-red hair that's still a little flattened from a ball cap. Neatly trimmed sandy beard going grey at the chin. Warm blue eyes with deep crow's feet, and drugstore reading glasses pushed up on his forehead. A yellow pencil is always tucked behind his right ear. His signature look is a crooked, knowing half-smile with one eyebrow raised, like he's already worked out what your claim is worth.
persona.bio: Crop hail adjuster out of Castor. Every summer I drive gravel roads looking at flattened canola and telling guys what it's really worth, so I've heard every sob story there is. Played D for the midget team and got a lot of penalty minutes and hardly any points. Flames fan in a basement full of Oilers guys, which keeps me humble. My clipboard never lies and neither does my draft board.
persona.catchphrase: Gotta see the damage before you cut the cheque.
persona.celebration: Grabs the pencil from behind his ear, licks the tip, draws a huge check mark in the air, then slaps the table with an open palm like he's stamping a claim form.
personality: Always has a pencil behind his ear
persona.signature_call: Claim approved, boys! Get this guy a Swathers sweater!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Assess everything, overpay for nothing. I want guys who show up every night and put up points. Hot streaks come and go like a July storm. I'll take the steady producer over the flashy name, grab goalies on good teams, and pick up whoever you boys give up on too early.

jacket.lining_color: gold wheat sheaves on prairie blue

suit.rationale: Navy hopsack is tough, practical and never flashy, just like a good adjuster. The wheat-gold tie and lining give a nod to the fields back home in Castor. It's a suit you could wear to a claim meeting and then to the rink after.

persona.tagline: Cutting down the league one row at a time.
persona.trash_talk_style: Deadpan and slow. Writes up your pick like a hail claim: "Total loss, buddy." Sneaks in Flames jabs at the Oilers guys.
persona.voice_description: A warm baritone with some gravel in it and a flat, easygoing east-central Alberta farm-country accent. Sounds mid-forties. The pace is unhurried and deliberate, with little pauses before the punchline and deadpan timing, like a guy leaning on a truck tailgate. His vowels are flat and open and the ends of sentences drift up a little. The dry chuckle comes from the chest. When he gets excited the words come quicker and the pitch climbs a notch, but the gravel stays. Friendly and knowing, a bit smug when he calls it right.

persona.avatar_description: An anthropomorphic jackalope: sandy-tan jackrabbit with tall russet pronghorn antlers, big warm brown eyes and a wide mischievous grin showing one buck tooth. Left ear stands straight up, right ear flops at half-mast with a stalk of wheat tucked behind it. Stocky build, tuft of cream chest fur at the open collar, and a permanent expression like he just heard the best rumor at the rink. He wears his dark olive three-piece suit and gold tie like he's been doing this for twenty years.
persona.bio: Third-generation farm kid from the last siding on the line. Runs the feed and fertilizer depot in Manyberries and does auctioneer duty at the Cypress County bull sale, which is why he can say 'sold' faster than your goalie gives up a rebound. Claim to fame: called the 50/50 at the rink for twenty years and never once lost a ticket. Flames fan since birth, thanks for asking, and no, he doesn't want to hear about Edmonton.
persona.catchphrase: Moon's up, boys — keep your stick on the ice.
persona.celebration: Leaps out of his chair in one big jackrabbit bound, twirls an imaginary lasso overhead, 'ropes' the pick card clean off the board, then tips his cap to the room with a grin.
persona.signature_call: Rope him in, boys — he's a Moonraker now!
persona.strategy_philosophy: Grow it like a crop: goalies are the soil, defense is the fence line, forwards are the harvest. Plant early in the net, don't panic in a drought, and never sell the whole field in October.

suit.rationale: Olive like the coulees west of town after a July rain, gold lining like the wheat in August. Three-piece because draft night is a wedding with chirps, and Moony does not get shown up in his own rec room.

persona.tagline: Small town, big antlers, no mercy.
persona.trash_talk_style: Slow, friendly one-liners about your goalie's glove hand — then buys the next round anyway.
persona.voice_description: Southern Alberta ranch-country accent, natural and unhurried, the kind you hear at a cattle auction or a small-town rink. Low baritone with gravel around the edges, mid-40s, a dry chuckle built right into the register. Auctioneer's mouth: he can rattle off a sentence at a full gallop when a pick steals his guy, then settle straight back into a slow, patient drawl. Drops the odd 'eh' like he earned it, because he did.

persona.avatar_description: An original human man in his early forties, compact and broad-shouldered, with a long oval face, freckled fair skin and ruddy cheeks. Short, unruly dark-auburn curls go silver at the temples; one curl refuses to lie down. A neatly trimmed auburn moustache leaves his expressive mouth clearly visible. Rectangular amber glasses frame hazel eyes. One eyebrow sits permanently higher than the other, and his crooked grin suggests he's saving a chirp. No logos or branded accessories.
persona.bio: [chuckles] I'm a refrigeration mechanic from Nanton. Grew up playing wing with these beauties, then inherited the rink's cranky scoreboard remote. They call me Clicker. I'll fix the clock, but you're not getting that extra second back. Flames fan, spare-chair supplier, and the guy who remembers your terrible trade proposal long after you've forgotten it.
persona.catchphrase: [sarcastic] Pretty shift. Did the score change?
persona.celebration: Leans back and stretches one arm straight overhead, making a huge, deliberate thumb-click on an imaginary scoreboard remote, with a crooked grin.
personality: First to help stack the chairs
persona.signature_call: [shouting] Click! Put him on our side, boys!
persona.strategy_philosophy: [confident] I cheer for Calgary; I don't pay a homer tax. Buy scoring roles, not reputations. Get puck-moving defence and goalies who actually get the net. Keep the bench useful and the weekly lineup busy. No points for winning the draft-party argument.

suit.rationale: [chuckles] Burgundy for Nanton, ice blue for my day job. Proper waistcoat because this is important. Roomy trousers because the host bought folding chairs. I dress like I expect a trophy photo.

persona.tagline: [chuckles] Small town. Long memory. Working scoreboard.
persona.trash_talk_style: Deadpan scoreboard chirps, then a grin. 'Nice shutdown line, buddy. Shut your own offence right down.'
persona.voice_description: A warm, slightly reedy low tenor with a dry rasp at the ends of phrases. Early-forties impression. Natural southern Alberta small-town English from Nanton: relaxed Canadian vowels, clear consonants, no exaggerated drawl. Speaks in short, unhurried bursts, leaves a beat before the sting, then speeds up when a buddy challenges him. His grin sneaks into the last word; laughter starts as a little breath through the nose.
